site.name: stripe-docs
site.summary: stripe-docs-clone Clone of the Stripe Docs Hosted Checkout Quickstart tutorial area. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Quickstart home: three-column layout — left product / section navigation tree, central step-by-step tutorial (each step: explanation + multi-language switchable code block + copy button + Test / Live markers), right-side on-this-page outline (scroll-spy highlighting); top Stripe docs nav (Docs / API reference / Search / environment switch) | | `embedded.html` | Embedded checkout variant: iframe / element integration steps for embedding into a site | | `customization.html` | Branding and customization: colors, logo, domain, email, etc. |

run_plan.goal: Explore the Stripe docs clone end-to-end across the hosted quickstart, embedded checkout, and customization pages, validating navigation, interactive doc controls, external references, and responsive behavior without assuming functionality beyond what the prescan shows.
run_plan.summary: Start on the hosted quickstart as the primary flow, then branch into embedded checkout and customization to confirm the adjacent tutorial paths and cross-links. Validate the visible controls that are actually present: top nav tabs, left-side section links, search, branding/open-source links, code block language switches, copy buttons, and any dialog-backed interactions. Repeat the critical checks in mobile viewport, with extra attention to tap targets and layout stability because several controls were flagged as small on mobile.
assumptions: The three local HTML pages are the full site surface available for this run.
External Stripe docs/dashboard links may open live sites, but the core local UX should still be validated from the clone.
The visible dialog on the pages is likely tied to a control such as search or a confirmation state, but its exact behavior should be discovered during exploration.
Code examples and step markers on the docs pages are interactive enough to test copying and language switching where present.
risk_hotspots: Top navigation controls on index.html, embedded.html, and customization.html: Hosted/Embedded/Customization tabs, Search button, Branding, and Open source links
Code block controls on the docs pages: language switch button(s) and multiple Copy buttons with small mobile tap targets
Right-side on-this-page outline / scroll-spy behavior on index.html, especially whether section highlighting tracks scroll correctly
External reference links to live Stripe docs and Dashboard pages, which may expose broken or misleading destinations
Mobile viewport tap targets flagged as small: home/logo link, Stripe Checkout breadcrumb/link, Copy buttons, Yes/No buttons, and reference links
Any search or dialog interaction because the prescan reports one dialog on each page but does not reveal the trigger

phases.title: Host quickstart baseline
phases.objective: Validate the main hosted Checkout tutorial flow and its primary in-page interactions on index.html.
key_checks: Confirm the hosted page loads with the expected three-column docs layout and top nav
Open and close the search control if it reveals a dialog or overlay
Exercise the left sidebar navigation and the main hosted content anchors
Click at least one code-language toggle and one Copy button in the hosted tutorial
Scroll through the page to verify outline/scroll-spy highlighting in the right rail
exit_criteria: Primary hosted flow visually and interactively confirmed
At least one code block interaction and one navigation interaction validated
No broken local-state behavior observed in the main content or sidebar

phases.title: Hosted adjacent flows and external references
phases.objective: Validate the hosted page’s adjacent flows and outbound references for correctness and consistency.
key_checks: Open the local links to Embedded payment form and Customize Checkout from the left nav and return to index.html
Check the top tabs for Hosted, Embedded, and Customization consistency
Open official external references such as Checkout overview, Webhook quickstart, Testing cards, Branding settings, and Official docs/Open source
Verify the local breadcrumb/section labeling remains accurate after navigation or return
exit_criteria: All local cross-links between the three pages have been traversed at least once from the hosted page
Several external links have been sampled and their destinations confirmed
No obvious mismatch between the page label and the visible hosted tutorial content

phases.title: Embedded checkout variant
phases.objective: Validate the embedded quickstart as a distinct flow with its own content, controls, and return-path framing.
key_checks: Confirm the embedded page content differs appropriately from hosted checkout and references ui_mode/embedded behavior
Exercise the embedded page’s visible code block interactions, copy controls, and any step markers
Check the local nav and top tabs for correct active-state behavior
Verify any return_url or resume-flow guidance is presented consistently with the embedded tutorial
exit_criteria: Embedded variant content is readable and functionally distinct from the hosted flow
At least one interactive control on the embedded page has been used successfully
Navigation back to the other local pages works from the embedded page

phases.title: Customization and policy surface
phases.objective: Validate what Checkout branding/customization actually allows and ensure the page does not overpromise unsupported controls.
key_checks: Confirm the page framing is reality-checked and focused on branding, text, policies, blocked card brands, and custom domains
Exercise any local controls present on the page, including code or option toggles and copy actions
Open relevant external references to Stripe docs or Dashboard branding settings
Check that claims about customization remain consistent with the visible controls
exit_criteria: Customization page content and scope align with its visible controls
At least one control and one outbound reference validated
No false impression of broad Checkout customization is introduced by the UI

phases.title: Responsive and mobile validation
phases.objective: Repeat critical interactions on mobile viewport and assess the flagged tap-target and layout risks.
key_checks: Re-open the three local pages in mobile viewport and confirm the main navigation still works
Test the smallest flagged tap targets, especially logo/home, Stripe Checkout link, Copy buttons, Yes/No buttons, and reference links
Verify the multi-column layout adapts acceptably without hiding essential content or controls
Check that search/dialog behavior remains usable on mobile
exit_criteria: Critical navigation and content remain usable on mobile
At least one representative small-tap-target issue has been confirmed or ruled out in context
No major mobile-only breakage prevents the docs flows from being explored

coverage_targets.features: exercise most visible controls per key page, including top nav, local side nav, search/dialog trigger, code language toggle, copy buttons, and selected external links
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks on mobile viewport, prioritizing flagged small tap targets and cross-page navigation

notes: Keep the run anchored to the local three-page docs clone; external Stripe links are supporting validation, not the main target.
Because the prescan shows no console or network errors, prioritize UX correctness, control behavior, and responsive usability over error recovery.

observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.

observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. observation.title: Stripe-hosted Checkout quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ line_items: [ { price: "price_12345", quantity: 1, }, ], mode: "payment", success_url: "http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url: "http://localhost:4242/cancel", }); res.redirect(303, session.url); }); app.listen(4242, () => { console.log("Listening on http://localhost:4242"); }); Key Session parame

observation.title: Stripe-hosted Checkout quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Python pip install stripe flask 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.PY Copy Showing Python import os import stripe from flask import Flask, redirect stripe.api_key = os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"] app = Flask(__name__) @app.post("/create-checkout-session") def create_checkout_session(): session = stripe.checkout.Session.create( line_items=[ { "price": "price_12345", "quantity": 1, } ], mode="payment", success_url="http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url="http://localhost:4242/cancel", ) return redirect(session.url, code=303) Key Session parameters for the hosted UI line_items The products or prices a customer is paying for. Stripe recommends usi

observation.title: Embedded Checkout page quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. observation.title: Stripe-hosted Checkout quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Python pip install stripe flask 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.PY Copy Showing Python import os import stripe from flask import Flask, redirect stripe.api_key = os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"] app = Flask(__name__) @app.post("/create-checkout-session") def create_checkout_session(): session = stripe.checkout.Session.create( line_items=[ { "price": "price_12345", "quantity": 1, } ], mode="payment", success_url="http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url="http://localhost:4242/cancel", ) return redirect(session.url, code=303) Key Session parameters for the hosted UI line_items The products or prices a customer is paying for. Stripe recommends usi

HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. TERMINAL Copy Showing Python pip install stripe flask 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and borde

observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and borde

observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #edf2ff BUTTON COLOR #89a7ff TEXT COLOR #f5f8ff FONT FAMILY Source Code Pro BORDER SHAPE 10px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family

observation.title: Embedded Checkout page quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Python pip install stripe flask Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.PY Copy Showing Python import os import stripe from flask import Flask, jsonify stripe.api_key = os.environ["STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"] app = Flask(__name__) @app.post("/create-checkout-session") def create_checkout_session(): session = stripe.checkout.Session.create( line_it

This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.

observation.title: Embedded Checkout page quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.

observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and borde

observation.title: Stripe-hosted Checkout quickstart | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ line_items: [ { price: "price_12345", quantity: 1, }, ], mode: "payment", success_url: "http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url: "http://localhost:4242/cancel", }); res.redirect(303, session.url); }); app.listen(4242, () => { console.log("Listening on http://localhost:4242"); }); Key Session parame

Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Hosted quickstart REBUILT GUIDE Build a Stripe-hosted checkout page that behaves like the real docs. This page now mirrors the current hosted Checkout flow: create a Checkout Session on your server, send a 303 redirect to session.url, and use webhooks for fulfillment instead of trusting the success page. Matches current Checkout Sessions guidance for the hosted UI. Every visible control on this page now does something real. Each “source” link points to Stripe’s live docs or Dashboard. WHAT CHANGED No more dead links or fake guidance The old page mixed accurate snippets with placeholder navigation and a few misleading claims. This rebuild keeps the visual style but replaces the broken shell with usable docs behavior. Hosted Default ui_mode for Checkout Sessions 303 Recommended server redirect after Session creation Webhook Reliable place to fulfill an order CHOOSE YOUR UI 0 Why start with the Stripe-hosted page The hosted UI is still the fastest way to ship Checkout. Stripe hosts the payment page, keeps the payment-method UX current, and can use a custom domain if you need the final checkout URL to look branded. HOSTED CHECKOUT Lowest integration effort Customers leave your app for a Stripe-hosted payment page, then return to your site after payment. You create a Session, redirect to session.url, and listen for events like checkout.session.completed. Best if you want the least custom frontend code. Supports Stripe-managed UI updates and custom domains. Great default when you do not need the payment form embedded in-page. EMBEDDED FORM Same Sessions API, more in-page control The embedded flow keeps customers on your site, but still uses Checkout Sessions and Stripe-hosted iframes for the secure payment UI. If you need that version, open the embedded guide in this rebuild. Uses ui_mode: 'embedded_page' and return_url. Mounted with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Still limited customization compared with a fully custom Elements build. SERVER EXAMPLES One language switch now controls every multi-language snippet on the page. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the Stripe server SDK Use Stripe’s official server-side library to create Checkout Sessions from your backend. The frontend doesn’t need Stripe.js for this hosted redirect flow. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express 2 Create a Checkout Session on your server Create the Session on the backend, set your line items and URLs, then redirect the customer to the hosted Checkout page. For hosted Checkout, success_url and cancel_url are the important return points. Hosted is the default Session mode The Checkout Sessions API defaults ui_mode to hosted, so you normally omit it here. That keeps this guide aligned with Stripe’s current hosted quickstart instead of mixing in embedded-only parameters. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ line_items: [ { price: "price_12345", quantity: 1, }, ], mode: "payment", success_url: "http://localhost:4242/success?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}", cancel_url: "http://localhost:4242/cancel", }); res.redirect(303, session.url); }); app.listen(4242, () => { console.log("Listening on http://localhost:4242"); }); Key Session parame

observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.

observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Embedded page CURRENT API FLOW Embed Stripe Checkout on your site without freezing the docs in an old API version. This rebuild follows Stripe’s current embedded quickstart: create a Session with ui_mode: 'embedded_page', return the client_secret, mount with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(), and use return_url to resume after redirect-based methods. Replaces stale ui_mode: 'embedded' examples with the current embedded page flow. Shows the exact difference between embedded Checkout and a fully custom Elements integration. Keeps all the utility features from the hosted flow, including working copy and search behavior. WHY EMBED Keep checkout on your domain while Stripe still owns the secure payment UI Customers stay on your page, but Stripe handles the iframe, the payment confirmation states, and the return path for redirect-based methods. embedded_page Current Checkout Session ui_mode client_secret Returned by the server and consumed by Stripe.js return_url Needed for redirect-based payment methods and retries DECISION POINT 0 When to use the embedded page instead of hosted or Elements Embedded Checkout is the middle ground. You keep the payment form in-page, but you still let Stripe manage the form lifecycle and most payment-method complexity. EMBEDDED PAGE Best when you want in-page checkout with low code Use the Checkout Sessions API plus Stripe.js. Your server returns a client_secret, and the client mounts the page with stripe.createEmbeddedCheckoutPage(). Customers stay on your site for the main payment step. Branding is still limited compared with fully custom Elements. Stripe handles redirect-based payment methods through the return_url. ELEMENTS Use only when you need deeper UI control Elements gives you the most control, but it also asks you to manage more UI state, layout, and integration details. Stripe positions Checkout Sessions plus Elements as a more advanced build. Custom layout and component composition. More code and more surface area to maintain. Recommended only if Checkout’s limited customization isn’t enough. SERVER EXAMPLES Switch the examples below without losing your place in the guide. Node Python Ruby PHP 1 Install the server SDK and load Stripe.js on the page The server still creates the Session, but the client now needs Stripe.js because Stripe mounts the embedded Checkout frame on your page. TERMINAL Copy Showing Node npm install stripe express Do not nest Checkout inside another iframe Stripe explicitly warns against placing embedded Checkout inside your own iframe because some payment methods need to redirect the customer to another page to complete confirmation. 2 Create an embedded Checkout Session on the server Create the Session server-side, set ui_mode: 'embedded_page', and return the Session’s client_secret to the client. For this flow, success_url is not allowed. Instead, use return_url. Why return_url still matters Even though the payment form is embedded, some payment methods still redirect the customer to an intermediate bank or wallet page. Stripe sends them back to your return_url and substitutes {CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID} so you can recover the Session state. SERVER.JS Copy Showing Node const express = require("express"); const Stripe = require("stripe"); const app = express(); const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY); app.post("/create-checkout-session", async (req, res) => { const session = await stripe.checkout.

observation.title: Customize Checkout | Stripe docs clone
observation.visible_text: stripe Docs clone Hosted Embedded Customization Official docs Search… / Branding Open source LOCAL REBUILD Hosted quickstart Embedded payment form Customize Checkout OFFICIAL REFERENCES Checkout overview Compare hosted and embedded Checkout flows. Webhook quickstart Handle post-payment events reliably. Testing cards Use Stripe's current test numbers and flows. Branding settings Manage Checkout branding in the Dashboard. WHY THIS CLONE EXISTS Every visible control is wired up, and every source link points to the live Stripe docs or Dashboard. Stripe Checkout / Customization REALITY-CHECKED Customize Checkout without inventing controls Stripe doesn’t actually offer. This page removes the fake “everything is configurable” framing and replaces it with the real Stripe Checkout surface: branding settings, branding_settings, text and policies, blocked card brands, custom domains for hosted pages, and product images from Products or inline product_data. Hosted Checkout and embedded page do not expose the same branding surface. Custom domains apply to Stripe-hosted pages, not to the embedded page on your own site. Policy text is flexible, but Stripe explicitly warns against creating ambiguous or non-compliant copy. CUSTOMIZATION LIMIT Checkout stays opinionated on purpose Stripe Checkout is meant to stay low-code and high-conversion. You can brand it, annotate it, and restrict certain payment details, but you cannot turn it into a fully bespoke checkout UI. 20 Preset font families Stripe documents for Checkout 3 Preset border radius shapes in Checkout branding 1,200 Maximum length Stripe documents for custom text blocks SCOPE CHECK 0 What Stripe Checkout actually lets you change Stripe Checkout offers limited customization. That is part of the product design. The safe mental model is: you can brand the shell, add policy and support details, tune some payment restrictions, and enrich the product context. If you need total layout control, Checkout probably isn’t the right tool. HOSTED PAGE Most complete branding surface The Stripe-hosted page can use your own logo or icon, custom colors, supported fonts, border style, business name, product images, legal policies, support details, and even a custom subdomain. Supports logo and icon in branding settings. Supports custom domains because Stripe hosts the checkout URL. Still limited to Stripe’s overall page structure. EMBEDDED PAGE Same policy tools, narrower visual surface The embedded page inherits the same general Checkout behavior but narrows some presentation controls. Stripe documents background color, button color, font, shapes, and display name, not a full logo-and-icon treatment inside the iframe. Uses the same branding_settings object with embedded-page-specific limits. Does not need a custom domain because it already renders on your site. Shares card-brand filtering, policies, and product-image behavior with hosted Checkout. 1 Appearance and branding settings Stripe documents two ways to brand Checkout: Dashboard settings and per-session branding_settings. If you omit a field in branding_settings, Checkout falls back to the Dashboard default. Hosted and embedded do not expose identical visual controls Stripe’s appearance docs show logo and icon controls on the hosted page, while the embedded page documentation centers on display name, background color, button color, font family, and border shape. Stripe-like Slate Earth Bright BACKGROUND COLOR #ffffff BUTTON COLOR #635bff TEXT COLOR #1a1f36 FONT FAMILY Inter BORDER SHAPE 14px Business Powdur Outfitters Email jenny@example.com Card details 4242 4242 4242 4242 Pay $20.00 Branding controls Stripe documents branding_settings.display_name Overrides the business name shown in Checkout. Stripe also lets you set the default in Business details. branding_settings.background_color and button_color Control the main surface and primary action color. If you skip them, Stripe uses your Dashboard defaults. branding_settings.font_family and borde
